observation: Held-out log loss 0.122 versus 0.229 for the model without predictors (improvement 0.106, a reduction by 47%); 10 of 10 folds improve.
relevance: A model description holds whatever the model's accuracy; the improvement provides the scale of the minimum importance.
summary: Held-out log loss 0.122 versus 0.229 for the model without predictors (improvement 0.106, a reduction by 47%); 10 of 10 folds improve

observation: R^2 on the other 26 predictors: self-rated health (A2) .19 and depressed mood (D2) .29; no named predictor reaches .50.
relevance: Dependence between predictors can redistribute marginal PFI between them; the R^2 of a predictor on all other predictors also detects dependence on several predictors jointly, and its R^2 on the predictors outside its group shows whether grouped PFI, which permutes only the members of the group jointly, accounts for it.
summary: R^2 on the other 26 predictors: self-rated health (A2) .19 and depressed mood (D2) .29; no named predictor reaches .50

property: On average over refits, XGBoost relies more on self-rated health (A2) than on depressed mood (D2).
criterion: Average over 10 folds: PFI of self-rated health (A2) above that of depressed mood (D2), beyond Monte Carlo error; the lower bound of the corrected 95% interval is at least 0.0011 (the smallest relevant difference); a reversal counts only if the upper bound is at most -0.0011.
observation: self-rated health (A2) 0.0463 versus depressed mood (D2) 0.0358; difference (PFI of self-rated health (A2) minus PFI of depressed mood (D2)) 0.0105 [0.0016, 0.0195].
relevance: The learner average over refits on 10 training sets of 15,274 rows is the quantity the claim names; selected from this average, the estimates are optimistic (winner's curse).
summary: on average, self-rated health (A2) 0.0463 versus depressed mood (D2) 0.0358 (difference 0.0105 [0.0016, 0.0195])

property: self-rated health (A2) matters relative to the accuracy of XGBoost.
criterion: self-rated health (A2) has a mean PFI of at least 1% of the improvement of XGBoost over the model without predictors (0.0011 log-loss units), beyond Monte Carlo error; a shortfall counts only if the upper bound of the corrected interval is below it.
observation: self-rated health (A2) 0.0463 versus the minimum importance 0.0011 (1% of the improvement of 0.106, from 0.229 to 0.122).
relevance: Ratios and ranks are scale-free; the minimum importance excludes negligible predictors.
summary: self-rated health (A2) has 0.0463, above the minimum importance 0.0011 (1% of the improvement)

property: The procedure computes the named quantity, and the wording is not broader than the scope.
criterion: Held-out marginal PFI as named in the scope; if grouped or conditional PFI reverses the result (beyond Monte Carlo error and the corrected interval), the wording names the marginal permutation.
observation: Held-out marginal PFI with log loss, 20 permutations per fold in 10 folds, as the scope names. No grouped or conditional comparison was requested.
relevance: Marginal permutation includes input combinations absent from the data; conditional and grouped PFI measure reliance on information a predictor does not share and on a group.
summary: held-out marginal PFI as the scope names; no grouped or conditional comparison was requested

property: The ordering recurs when XGBoost is refitted on other folds.
criterion: self-rated health (A2) has the larger PFI in at least 9 of 10 folds; a failing fold counts only beyond Monte Carlo error and by at least the smallest relevant difference (0.0011).
observation: self-rated health (A2) exceeds depressed mood (D2) in 9 of 10 folds; 1 other is within Monte Carlo error or below the smallest relevant difference.
relevance: Refits on other folds and new permutations estimate the same learner PFI again; on the data that suggested the claim, this share remains optimistic.
summary: self-rated health (A2) exceeds depressed mood (D2) in 9 of 10 folds; 1 other is within Monte Carlo error or below the smallest relevant difference
